transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place, and I appreciate your time. 

I guess... I'm mostly here because I just don't really feel like myself anymore. It's probably nothing too serious, just a bit of a rut, I guess. I mean, I used to be pretty active—hiking, coaching, playing my guitar... but I've sort of stopped doing all of that. I haven't even been calling people back lately. 

I don't want you to think I'm just lazy or anything, it's just... well, honestly, some days I just sit in my small rental for hours. I know there are things I need to do, but I just can't seem to make myself start. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
How long have you been feeling this way and noticing this loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Well, it's... I guess it's been a little while now. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, but things sort of started, um, unraveling, I guess you could say, after my divorce. 

I had to move into this smaller rental, and that was about... maybe a year and two months ago? I think that's when I really started to notice I wasn't keeping up with my guitar or the coaching as much. It's just been an adjustment, you know? Moving and all that. I'm sure a lot of people go through a slump after a big change like that, right? I just hope I'm explaining it okay.
Over this past year or so, would you say you've felt down, sad, or empty nearly every day, for most of the day?

I wouldn't say I feel sad or down every single day. I mean, I have good days too, you know? It's not like I'm crying all the time or completely miserable. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself. 

It's more just... empty, I guess? Like I'm just going through the motions sometimes. But I wouldn't call it depressed or anything like that. I'm sure it's just a normal reaction to everything that's happened. Does that sound like a normal way to react to a divorce and moving? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Besides feeling empty or going through the motions, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, energy level, or ability to concentrate over this past year?

Um, sleep and appetite? Well, I think I sleep okay. I mean, maybe I wake up a little early sometimes, but nothing major. I hope that's not a big deal. As for my appetite, I eat. Maybe I'm not cooking big meals like I used to, but I'm definitely eating. 

Energy... well, I mentioned I'm not hiking or anything, so I guess my energy is a little lower, but I'm still getting by. And my concentration is fine, I think. I can still read a book or watch TV. I hope I'm answering this right. I just don't think there's been any huge, dramatic changes with those things, you know? Is that what you were asking?

Over this past year, has there ever been a period of at least two weeks where things felt noticeably worse than your usual baseline—like your mood, sleep, or energy really dropped more severely—compared to how you've been describing things generally?

I don't... I don't think so. Not like a sudden, terrible crash or anything. I mean, sure, some weeks are a little tougher than others, maybe I feel a bit more tired or just kind of... blank, you know? But I always manage to pull it together. I wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything like that. 

I really try to keep things steady. I hope that makes sense. Is it normal to just have a bad week here and there without it being a big, serious problem? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information.
Before your divorce and the move, had you been feeling this kind of low, empty mood for a long time, or did this feeling really start only after those events happened?

Um, no, I don't think it was before. Before the divorce, things were... they were fine. I was always pretty steady. I mean, in my line of work, you kind of have to be, right? You just keep your head down, do the job, and stay strong. So, no, I wasn't feeling empty or anything back then. 

It really just seemed to creep up after the marriage ended and I had to pack up and relocate. That's a pretty normal time to feel a little off, isn't it? Just with all the stress of moving and everything. I just hope I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is. I was completely fine before all those changes happened, I promise. Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Over this past year, has there been any stretch of two months or more where you felt completely back to your normal self, without that empty or 'going through the motions' feeling?

Um... two months? I, uh, I guess not a full two months, no. But I definitely have good days! I mean, it's not like I'm walking around like a zombie every single minute. I have days where I feel pretty okay, where I go to work and get things done and it feels almost normal. 

I just... maybe the 'okay' days don't string together for a whole two months straight without a little bit of that empty feeling creeping back in. But that's probably to be expected, right? With everything that happened? I mean, nobody is perfectly happy all the time. I just want to make sure you know I'm really trying my best to stay positive. I'm not just giving up or anything. Does that sound like a normal reaction to you?

Since the divorce and move happened about 14 months ago, would you say the situation itself—like legal matters, finances, or living arrangements—has been fully settled for a while now, or is it still an active, unresolved stressor in your life?

Well, I mean, it's mostly settled. The paperwork is done, and I've been in the new place for a while now. There's always a little bit of, you know, financial stuff to figure out when you're on a single income again, but it's really nothing I can't handle. 

I don't want you to think I'm constantly stressing over it or letting it ruin my life. I go to work, I pay my bills, I keep the place clean. It's just... normal life stuff, right? Everyone has to deal with bills and budgets. It's not like an active crisis or anything like that. I'm doing a pretty good job managing it all, I think. Does that make sense? I just want to be clear that I'm keeping on top of my responsibilities.
Over this past year, have you often felt hopeless about the future or noticed a drop in your self-esteem or confidence in yourself?

Um, no, I wouldn't say hopeless. Not at all. I mean, sure, starting over is a bit of an adjustment, but I always try to keep looking forward, you know? And as for my confidence... I think I'm still the same guy. In my line of work, you really can't afford to second-guess yourself out there, so I always make sure I'm squared away and ready to handle whatever comes up. 

I still take a lot of pride in what I do, and I haven't lost that. I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression here. I'm not sitting around feeling sorry for myself or thinking the future is bleak. I'm actually trying to be pretty optimistic, all things considered. I still believe things will turn out fine. Does that sound like I'm handling it okay to you? I really am trying to keep a good attitude about everything.

Just to pin down the timeline clearly—has this low, empty feeling been going on continuously for two full years or longer, or would you say it's been less than two years, closer to the 14 months since your divorce and move?

Oh, definitely not two full years. No, it hasn't been that long at all. I'd say it really just started when I moved into the smaller rental after the divorce, so... yeah, about a year and two months ago. Fourteen months sounds exactly right. Before that, everything was completely fine. 

And even since the move, like I said, I've been keeping things together. I know it might sound like things have been unraveling a bit since the divorce, but I really just view it as an adjustment period, you know? Getting used to the smaller place, the new routine... it just takes a little time to bounce back completely. Does that timeline seem pretty standard to you? I mean, for someone going through a big life change like that, it's normal that it takes a little over a year to fully adjust, right?

Has this low, empty feeling or your reduced activity level caused any real problems at work, or with your relationships and daily responsibilities—like missing work, conflicts with others, or falling behind on things you need to do?

Well, um... I guess it has caused a few bumps, but nothing I can't come back from. I mean, I did... I did get suspended from my protective service job recently. But it was just a misunderstanding, really. I was on a routine patrol and I guess I... I might have come across a little intense? Some of the staff and bystanders got a bit spooked, but I was just trying to do my job, you know? Be thorough. I'm sure it'll get sorted out soon. 

And, uh, because of the suspension and everything else, I have stepped back a little bit from... well, from coaching and volunteering. I just figured I needed a minute to catch my breath and get my own house in order, so to speak. I haven't been seeing the people who usually count on me as much, but that's just temporary. I just didn't want to bring any of my stress into those situations, which is the responsible thing to do, right? Taking a step back to refocus? I'm hoping to get right back to it once this suspension is cleared up. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Can you tell me more about what happened during that patrol—were you feeling unusually irritable, on edge, or angry in the moments leading up to it?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I was angry. Not at all. I try really hard to keep an even keel, especially on the job. You have to, right? 

I mean, maybe I was a little... focused? Like, really dialed in to making sure everything was secure. I wasn't snapping at anyone or losing my temper, I promise. I just... I wanted to make sure I wasn't missing anything, and sometimes when you're concentrating that hard, people misread it. They think you're on edge when you're really just being diligent. 

I definitely wasn't trying to scare anybody or be difficult. I always try to be professional. Does that make sense? That it was just me trying to do a really thorough job and it maybe just looked a little intense from the outside?
Can you walk me through exactly what you said or did during that patrol that made the staff and bystanders react the way they did?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, looking back, I can see how it might have seemed a little unusual to them. I was just trying to be really careful, you know? 

I... I guess I started reacting to things a bit faster than I usually do, before I could really slow myself down and explain what I was doing. Like, I crouched behind some of the counters, just to check the sightlines and make sure it was secure. And I was... I was signaling for people to stay back, just for their own safety, really. 

And, um, I might have been repeating some of the things people were saying. Just the last few words. I was just trying to process if... if they were involved in anything, you know? Just being thorough. And I did pace the same route a few times. I just wanted to make absolutely sure the perimeter was clear. 

I think that's when the staff started looking a little scared of me, which I feel terrible about. I really didn't mean to frighten anyone. I was just doing my best to protect them. That's understandable, right? Sometimes when you're just trying to be really good at your job, it can come across the wrong way to people who don't do security work?
During that patrol, did it feel like you were suddenly reliving or reacting to a specific past event or experience, almost as if it were happening again in that moment?

No, oh no, it wasn't like that. I wasn't... I wasn't having a flashback or anything like that, if that's what you mean. 

I know some guys who have been through some really tough things, and they get like that, where they think they're back in a bad situation. But that wasn't me. I was completely in the present moment, just... just trying to do my job right there in the building. I knew exactly where I was and what time it was. 

I just wanted to make sure everyone was safe right then and there. I wasn't confused about that at all. Does that make sense? I promise I wasn't losing touch with where I was. I was just trying to be a good employee, you know?

Have you ever experienced or witnessed an event where you felt your life or someone else's life was seriously threatened—such as violence, a severe accident, or combat exposure—at any point in your life, including in your line of work?

No, I... I haven't. I mean, I've seen some scuffles, you know, just regular security stuff. Someone gets a little loud, maybe they need to be escorted out. But nothing... nothing crazy. No weapons or, you know, life-or-death situations. 

I've always been pretty lucky, I guess, or maybe just good at de-escalating things before they get to that point. I try really hard to keep things calm. I've never been in combat or a terrible car crash or anything like that. Just a normal, quiet life, really. 

I know some people in my line of work have seen some awful things, and I have so much respect for them, but I've managed to avoid all that. Is that what you were looking for? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

Aside from that patrol incident, have you ever had other moments—at work or elsewhere—where you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings, like you were watching yourself from outside, or where you couldn't fully remember what happened afterward?

No, no, I've never had anything like that happen. I've always been really, um, present, I guess you could say. I don't space out or lose time or anything like that. 

I mean, sometimes I get really focused on my work, but I always know exactly what I'm doing and I remember it all perfectly fine. I've never felt like I was outside my body or anything strange like that. I'm just a regular guy who tries to do a good job. 

I hope that's a good thing, right? That I don't have those kinds of problems? I really try to stay grounded and focused. I'm answering these questions okay, aren't I? I just want to be helpful.

During that patrol, did you notice anything unusual with your senses—like hearing sounds or voices that others didn't seem to notice, or feeling unusually suspicious that people around you meant you harm?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I hear things in a bad way. Not like how people mean it when they're... you know, unwell. I'm completely fine, I promise. It's just... well, I guess I should be completely honest with you, since I want to be helpful. 

Because of my job, I'm so used to the equipment, right? So sometimes, even when my radio scanner is completely turned off, I'll hear these... like, short little radio-like voices. Just quick bursts, usually warning me that someone is inside the building, or telling me that I'm being watched. It's probably just my brain playing tricks because I'm trying so hard to be thorough and do a good job, you know? 

And, um... sometimes at home, I might see a shadow move past the hallway. Just a quick movement, even after I've already done a full sweep and cleared every single room. But that's just my security training kicking in, right? Just being hyper-vigilant? 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound... strange. I know it sounds a little weird saying it out loud, but I'm just trying to be a good employee and keep things safe. That's a normal thing to happen when you work in security, isn't it? I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression of me.

How long have you been noticing these radio-like voices and shadow movements—did they start around the same time as the empty, low mood feelings after your divorce, or were they happening even during times when your mood felt fairly normal?

Well, um... it hasn't been forever or anything. I've been doing my best to just push through it and do my job. I guess... if I'm being completely honest, because I want to give you the right information... the little radio voices, and the shadows, and... well, that fixed feeling I get that people are tracking my movements... it's been happening for about four months now. 

And, um, my mood has actually been fairly normal during a lot of that time. It wasn't just when I was feeling low about the divorce. I've been getting up, going to work, doing my sweeps... just trying to be reliable, you know? 

Four months isn't that long of a time, right? I'm sure it's just a temporary thing from working so hard and wanting to be thorough. I really hope you don't think I'm... well, that there's something seriously wrong with me. I'm still doing my job well, I promise. I answered that okay, didn't I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.

Do you ever notice that same feeling of being watched, or hear those brief voice-like sounds, when you're not working—like at home with friends, or in situations that have nothing to do with security?

Well, um... yes, I guess I do. I mean, I want to be completely open with you, so... yes, it happens at home, too. Like I said before, sometimes when I'm just at my house, I'll see a shadow dart past the hallway. And that's even after I've done a full sweep of the house and made sure every single room is clear. 

And the radio voices... yeah, they happen when I'm not at work, too. Just those short little bursts, like a scanner, warning me about someone being inside or telling me I'm being watched. Even when I don't have my equipment anywhere near me. 

But I really think it's just because my brain is so trained to be on high alert, you know? Like, I'm just so dedicated to being a good security worker that I can't turn it off when I get home. It's just my work ethic bleeding over into my personal life. That shows I'm dedicated, right? I really hope you don't think it means I'm crazy or anything. I'm just trying to be a good, responsible person. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications/supplements around the time these voices and shadow sightings began four months ago?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um... I know sometimes people might turn to things like that if they're feeling stressed, but I really don't. Because of my security job, I have to stay completely clean anyway, you know? But even without that, I just wouldn't touch any of that stuff. 

No recreational drugs at all, and I don't really drink. And no new medications or supplements either. I just try to stay healthy on my own. I want to make sure my mind is as sharp as possible so I can be reliable at work and do my sweeps properly. It's really important to me to be a responsible person, and I wouldn't want anything to jeopardize that. 

I'm doing the right thing by staying away from all that, aren't I? I really pride myself on being clean and dependable. I just want to make sure I'm taking care of myself exactly the way I'm supposed to.
